# Routing design

## 1. Current state of `@route`

```scala
// common/.../routes/Annotations.scala
final class route(val filePath: String, val method: String = "GET") extends StaticAnnotation

// bbs/.../Main.scala
@route("[bbs]/index.ts")
@JSExportTopLevel("boardIndexHandler", "server")
def boardIndexHandler(c: js.Any): js.Promise[Response] = BoardHandler.index(c.asInstanceOf[HonoContextFacade])
```

Generated output (`app/routes/[bbs]/index.ts`):

```ts
// This file is generated by codegen (io._3ch.codegen.GenerateAppFiles) from @route / @islands.
// …
import { createRoute } from "honox/factory";
// @ts-expect-error scalajs:server.js is a virtual module (see vite.config.ts).
import { boardIndexHandler } from "scalajs:server.js";

export default createRoute((c) => boardIndexHandler(c));
```

- `filePath` is relative to `app/routes`, and the URL is determined by HonoX's file conventions (`[bbs]` → `:bbs`, `index` → the directory, `[...x]` → `:x{.+}`, `(group)` → removed).
- Writing several `@route`s with different methods for the same `filePath` combines them into one file with `export default` (GET) and `export const POST = …`.
- Handlers receive Hono's Context as-is. Extracting parameters (`c.req.param("bbs")`) and validation are the handler's job.
- 3ch has 5 generated routes. They coexist with hand-written routes that pass to the existing fetch (`index.ts`, `admin/index.ts`, `auth.js.ts`, `bbsmenu.html.ts`)
  and with `app.get` / `app.post` / `app.all("*")` written directly in `app/server.ts`.

### 1.1 What codegen currently validates

Checks in `framework/AnnotationScanner`, `OutputPath` and `OutputWriter` (reference commit `875a47b`):

| Check | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Target | Exactly one `object Main`. Only the `def` / `val` directly under it |
| Export | Annotated declarations have exactly one `@JSExportTopLevel`. Its arguments are two string literals, and the moduleID is `server` (`@route`) / `client` (`@islands`) |
| Export name | Valid as a JS identifier (`[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*`) |
| Arguments | String literals only. Named arguments allowed only in declaration order |
| Path | Ends with `.ts`. Each segment is non-empty, not `.` or `..`, and matches `[A-Za-z0-9_.$\[\]-]+` |
| Method | `GET` / `POST` / `PUT` / `DELETE` / `PATCH` / `OPTIONS` / `HEAD` |
| Conflicts | Paths that differ only in case, duplicates with the same path and the same method |
| Route file names | Rejected if the basename starts with `_` (because HonoX's `ROUTES` excludes it). A leading `-` / `$`, `.test.ts` / `.spec.ts` and directories starting with `-` pass (1.2) |
| Island file names | Rejected if the basename doesn't match `[A-Za-z0-9-]+\.tsx` (HonoX `createClient`'s discovery rule; a P0 public rule, [rendering-model.md](rendering-model.md) 1.4) |
| Writing | Existing files without the generated banner are never overwritten or deleted (`OutputWriter`). All errors are collected before writing |

### 1.2 Current problems

| Problem | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `HEAD` | The current `HttpMethod` allows `HEAD`. HonoX's `createApp` looks only at `METHODS = [GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH]`, so `export const HEAD` is not registered. Hono's GET handler also answers HEAD, so rejecting `HEAD` is correct |
| File names HonoX ignores | `_*`, `-*`, `$*`, `*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts` and anything under `-*/` fall outside the `ROUTES` glob. The current check rejects only basenames starting with `_` and lets the rest through |
| URL-level conflicts | `foo.ts` and `foo/index.ts`, or `[a].ts` and `[b].ts`, are different files but the same URL pattern. The current check looks only at file paths |
| Conflicts with hand-written routes | A "same-named file" as a hand-written file is rejected, but a hand-written file with the same URL is not detected |
| Types | The handler argument is `js.Any`. Neither Env nor Context has a type |

## 2. Extension policy

### 2.1 Annotations

P0 doesn't change the shape of the arguments (`@route(filePath, method = "GET")`). Only the package moves to `hx4s.annotation`.

| Item | P0 | Candidates for P1 and later |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP methods | `GET` / `POST` / `PUT` / `DELETE` / `PATCH` / `OPTIONS`. `HEAD` is an error at generation time | `ALL` (outputs `createHono()` + `app.all`, the shape of 3ch's hand-written `index.ts`). U-13 |
| Multiple methods on one path | Combined into one file, as now | — |
| Dynamic parameters | Codegen extracts `[name]` / `[...name]` from the file path and checks that they are valid identifiers | Typed extraction (chapter 4) |
| How methods are written | Strings | An idea to also accept a `HttpMethod` enum. Since it is read by syntax analysis, only limited forms like `HttpMethod.Post` would be accepted |

### 2.2 What codegen validates (added in P0)

- Remove `HEAD` from the methods.
- Reject file names HonoX doesn't turn into routes (leading `_` / `-` / `$`, `.test.ts` / `.spec.ts`, directories starting with `-`).
- Implement the equivalent of `filePathToPath` in Scala and reject conflicts in **URL patterns** between generated routes. Patterns that differ only in parameter names count as conflicts.
  **Implemented (Phase 3 review K8)**: `hx4s.codegen.RoutePath`. It is an error only for the same method (different methods may share a URL). Rules and examples are under "URL conflicts" in [codegen.md](codegen.md).
- Run hand-written files (without the banner) under `app/routes` through the same conversion and warn on URL conflicts (a warning first, since rejecting would block intentional overrides by hand; U-23).
  **Not implemented** (no warning either).
- Print the number and list of generated routes to standard output in a deterministic order (so that diffs can be followed in review).
- Reject island basenames that don't match `[A-Za-z0-9-]+\.tsx` (implemented; a P0 public rule, [rendering-model.md](rendering-model.md) 1.4).

The conversion rules of `filePathToPath` follow HonoX's internal implementation (`server/utils/file.js`), so they are checked with compatibility tests every time HonoX is upgraded
([compatibility.md](compatibility.md) chapter 3).

### 2.3 What is left to HonoX

- Mapping to URLs, parsing parameters, route priority (ordering that puts names starting with `[` later, etc.).
- Trailing slashes (`createApp({ trailingSlash })`).
- Applying `_renderer` / `_middleware` / `_404` / `_error`. hx4s doesn't generate these files.
- Mixing generated and hand-written routes. hx4s doesn't forbid hand-written routes.

### 2.4 Consistency with file-based routing

hx4s keeps no route table of its own and limits `@route` to declaring "which file to generate". The reasons:

- HonoX's conventions (hierarchical application of renderers and middleware) can be used as-is. With our own route table, hx4s would have to reimplement them.
- The generated files are ordinary HonoX routes, so reading them tells you how they behave. Migrating to or mixing with hand-written routes is easy.

The trade-off is the inconvenience of writing file paths instead of URLs. P1 will consider a helper that works backwards from URLs (something like `@route.get("/:bbs/")`), but
it isn't in P0, because the same URL can correspond to several files depending on the mapping between `index.ts` and directories, and on `trailingSlash`.

## 3. Typed Context (P0)

Put a generic Hono Context facade in `hx4s-react`, with Env as a type parameter.

The Phase 3 implementation is `hx4s.hono.Context[Env, R <: js.Object]` (R is the renderer props passed to `c.render`) and `hx4s.hono.HonoRequest` (`raw: org.scalajs.dom.Request`, `param` / `query` / `header` / `method` / `url` / `path`);
`Context` has `res`, `header`, `status`, `text`, `json`, `redirect`, `render` and the extension method `renderPromise`. The facade is named `HonoRequest` so that it isn't confused with scalajs-dom's `Request`.

Following what was missing when the first user switched over in Phase 4, the following were added ([reviews/phase4-feedback.md](reviews/phase4-feedback.md)).

| Addition | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `Context.executionCtx: hx4s.hono.ExecutionContext` | A facade with only `waitUntil(promise)` and `passThroughOnException()`. Hono's `executionCtx` is a getter that throws `Error("This context has no ExecutionContext")` if the runtime didn't provide one (`dist/context.js` of hono 4.13.18). This facade also becomes a `js.JavaScriptException` on access |
| Extension method `executionCtxOption: Option[ExecutionContext]` | Turns the exception above into `None`, so the same handler runs in calls that don't provide an execution context, such as SSR verification on Node or `app.request()` |
| `Context.html`, `set` / `get` and the extension methods `setVariable` / `getVariable` (`ContextVariable[A]`) | `set` / `get` keep Hono's names and a `js.Any` interface. For typed reads and writes, define one `ContextVariable[A]("name")` and share it between both sides |
| `Context.body`, `notFound` | Added while writing the user documentation. `body(null, 204)` returns `204` / `304` without a body. `notFound()` is the response of the app's Not Found handler |
| `HonoRequest.queries`, `text()`, `json()`, `formData()` | Hono caches the body it read, so these can't be used after the body of `raw` has been read directly |

`ExecutionContext` is a minimal trait rather than a type parameter for these reasons:

- Adding a type parameter would change every place that writes the existing `Context[Env, R]`. Situations that use runtime-specific differences (Cloudflare's `props`, `exports`, etc.) are rare.
- hx4s's modules don't depend on Cloudflare types ([ADR 0005](adr/0005-core-independent-of-cloudflare.md)). Users who need runtime-specific members define their own `@js.native` trait extending `ExecutionContext` and cast to it.
- It is named `ExecutionContext` to match Hono. When used in the same file as `scala.concurrent.ExecutionContext`, give one an import alias.

Below is the Phase 0 proposal.

```scala
package hx4s.hono

@js.native
trait Request extends js.Object {
  val raw: org.scalajs.dom.Request = js.native   // U-6: the idea of using scalajs-dom's Fetch types
  def param(name: String): js.UndefOr[String] = js.native
  def query(name: String): js.UndefOr[String] = js.native
  def header(name: String): js.UndefOr[String] = js.native
}

@js.native
trait Context[Env] extends js.Object {
  val req: Request = js.native
  val env: Env = js.native
  def header(name: String, value: String): Unit = js.native
  def render(children: React.Element, props: js.UndefOr[js.Object] = js.native): org.scalajs.dom.Response | js.Promise[org.scalajs.dom.Response] = js.native
}
```

- 3ch's `HonoContextFacade` has `env: WorkerEnv` fixed and the props of `render` fixed to `RenderProps` (3ch's `title` / `authModal`). In hx4s, the user decides both.
  Renderer props are defined in a pair with `app/renderer.d.ts` (on the TS side), so hx4s has only a type parameter or an upper bound of `js.Object`.
- The generated route TS can stay `(c) => handler(c)`. On the Scala side, handlers can be written as `def handler(c: Context[MyEnv]): js.Promise[Response]`
  (the argument types of functions exported with `@JSExportTopLevel` aren't visible from JS, so changing `js.Any` to a typed one doesn't change the generated files).

## 4. Typed routes and a Client Router (P1 design proposal)

This chapter is a proposal and is not implemented in P0.

### 4.1 The double-maintenance problem

Within SSR + Islands, `<a href>` strings are enough for links. As SPA + API and API calls from islands increase,
the server routes (file paths of `@route`) and the client's URL strings are written separately, and mismatches aren't caught at compile time.

### 4.2 Proposal: make route definitions in shared the single source of truth

As `hx4s-routing` (P1), provide route definitions shared between JVM and JS.

```scala
// shared
object Routes {
  val board = Route.path("/" / Param.string("bbs") / "")          // :bbs
  val authAccount = Route.path("/auth/account/")
}
```

- Server: reference them with something like `@route.of(Routes.board)` instead of `@route`, and codegen derives the file path from **the syntax of the definition** of `Routes.board`.
  This is limited to what syntax analysis can follow (combinations of literals and a fixed DSL). If full semantic analysis is needed, reconsider moving to Scala 3 macros ([ADR 0004](adr/0004-scalameta-codegen.md)).
- Client: build URLs with the same `Routes.board(bbs = "news")`. Used for both island links and API calls.
- Handlers: get typed parameters with `Routes.board.params(c)`.

### 4.3 Comparison of Client Routers

| Aspect | scalajs-react Router (the `extra` module) | React Router (npm, with a facade) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dependencies | Just add scalajs-react's `extra`. Matches AGENTS.md's "prefer Scala.js libraries over npm" | Requires npm dependencies and maintaining a facade |
| Use with SSR | Thin support for SSR. Designed with SPAs in mind (a guess; details not investigated) | v7 has server rendering and data loading, but integration with Hono / HonoX would be our own |
| Fit with Islands | A Router per island splits state. The usage becomes one island covering the whole page in SPA mode | Same as left |
| Sharing route definitions | They are Scala values, so building from the definitions in 4.2 is easy | A layer converting definitions into JS objects is needed |
| Types | Can be expressed with Scala types | Depends on the facade |

Proposed policy: make scalajs-react Router the first candidate for the Client Router in SPA mode, and put an adapter that builds `RouterConfig` from the route definitions of 4.2 in `hx4s-routing`.
Consider a facade for React Router once users ask for it. Either way, the server side stays as HonoX file routes,
and codegen outputs the route that returns the SPA shell (a catch-all like `[...path].ts`).
